# FQE unified project integration — 2026-11-15

Status: native authoring verified; application project/replay foundation implemented and automatically verified; five-stage page integration and current bundled native UI journey remain pending. This is a current implementation note for `desk-fqe-product-integration-design.md`, not a claim that the discussion design is fully delivered. FQE task P4-03.03 remains IN_PROGRESS.

The first-party FQE authoring frontend owns the structured `strategy.fqe` language, descriptor-driven native lowering, source locations and lossless printing of its supported Event subset. `catalog.describe/1` discovers the contextual native node directory without a model. `authoring.event/1` supplies inspect/print. Python/Java/Go modules, Workflow/module authoring, optimizer controls, new package migration and long-history scale gates remain separately planned; the present desktop financial source limit is still256 bars. Clients receive the helper inside the application and need no Rust/compiler installation.

`lib/app/quant/fqe/authoring.dart` introduces `FqeAuthoringProject`. Its cryptographically random project ID survives renaming. A saved source buffer can remain invalid while the last valid source is retained; pending/invalid text blocks running the old model. Native results publish only when the expected project revision and generation still match. Graph edits print and inspect natively before one atomic install, retain comments and reject pending text conflicts. Native canonical execution identity plus ordered policies determines semantic revision; comments/layout do not change it. Research settings cannot contain a second model or policy set. The initial language prints retained comments as a leading block, preserving their contents/order rather than original inline placement.

`freeze()` returns copies of exact model, bindings, policies, history/range/warmup/account costs and an outer project/revision/generation/native-identity association. Mutating a caller copy cannot change the frozen input. `requireCurrent` rejects stale confirmation after any source/binding/configuration change. The application service repeats this guard after native preflight and after accepted-input storage, before admitting the native job. The association is persisted beside the raw native input/result and never inserted into native IR. The original `start(input, name:...)` API is preserved; project flows use `startProject`. Optional extensions check the actual hello capabilities and fail explicitly on an older helper.

The application service owns open project objects, creation, snapshot persistence and restoration. Already open project state cannot be replaced by a late restored snapshot. New `project` immutable records share the existing atomic/hash-verified store, with64 project snapshots and the existing total byte/file budgets; reaching a quota rejects without deleting history. There is no automatic pruning or migration. The existing global legacy editor state still exists for its old panel and is not the new project authority.

`replay.dart` builds a read-only projection from a hash-verified result. It validates the known cash-long native execution profile and exact command receipt schedule. Frames distinguish initial, incoming open-fill, closed strategy/policy and terminal cleanup, using authoritative receipt account views and native close-sampled equity. Open-phase equity is unavailable; it is never synthesized from candle prices. Playback has no RPC/evaluator and does not recompute a ledger. Damaged/missing/unknown results/cursors reject. Margin replay requires a separately verified adapter; raw margin results are not reinterpreted as this cash schedule.

Current paired candidate: FQE evidence commit704288e03a9906339d0d8087f0aaf81544cf01fa, bridge sha256:1f9c3ba7ff463d4227c6b25318776487bca2eb370d7e647419639d304c408201, Release helper SHA25683ca265dde194744f60323f856aa551beab4dadec5e723ef871a2d312e2602b7. `ci/fqe-engine.json` pins source bytes and the prepared helper; notices/financial engine/dependencies are unchanged. Preparation and temporary-app signing/staging pass. The already running Desk application was not rebuilt or restarted, so its installed helper may remain the earlier candidate. No current native UI claim follows from preparation.

Checks use the existing Flutter3.24.1/Dart3.5.1 caches and no Pub downloads. `test/fqe_authoring_check.dart ENGINE_ROOT OUTPUT_JSON [EXPLICIT_PEER]` exercises the actual Desk service and native process over11 checks: blank discovery, stable IDs, deep freeze/layout independence, graph/text round-trip/stale confirmation, restore conflict/comment-only identity, invalid-buffer persistence/recovery, native run association, two variants and immutable history, read-only replay, late native response and post-preflight change. Independent cases: SMA2/3 crosses5/7, fills6@4 and8@2, initial100→98; equal SMA3/3 never crosses and retains100. Replay separately checks open6 cash96/qty1, close6 equity98/close7 equity97, open8 cash98/qty0. Existing service/store and12 Flutter regressions are also run. Full native regression is354 Rust/23 external tests.

Next: wire these app-owned project objects into existing project selection, graph/code/parameter stages and existing backtest/results/replay content. Preserve workspace/panel/navigation IDs and FullDesktopDialog. Existing name-derived project IDs and independently editable legacy graph/Python documents must remain explicitly legacy until migration is implemented. Do not silently claim a unified current editor from this new library. Actual current-bundle offline/no-login, run/stop/two variants/reopen/active quit and stale interaction checks remain required. Shared editor/dashboard files are being modified concurrently; coordinate before native UI changes and do not overwrite unrelated edits.
